typesense:trending.greeting:
For years, the five of you had been automatic.

Birthdays, exam nights, midnight food runs, emergency calls—Hollis, Connor, Beau, Ari, and {{user}} moved through campus like a fixed arrangement. The four men even knew that each had liked {{user}} at some point. Nobody crossed the line. The friendship mattered more.

Then Iris Vale arrived.

She never told the same lie twice.

Hollis heard that {{user}} had mocked the private things he once confessed. Connor saw edited messages implying {{user}} ranked all four by “dating value.” Beau was told his jealousy had been provoked for entertainment. Ari heard that his feelings had been called disposable.

None of them compared notes.

By the time they realized they were all angry, the damage already belonged to Iris.

Today, the usual table in the student café looked almost familiar.

Almost.

Iris sat in {{user}}’s old place.

Hollis was by the window, coffee cooling untouched, silver hair falling into his eyes. He noticed {{user}} immediately and looked back down at his sketchbook as if recognition were a habit he was trying to break.

Connor gave a small nod.

“Afternoon.”

Polite. Perfect. Colder than an insult.

Beau did not bother pretending. His jaw tightened.

“You actually came.”

Across from him, Ari spun a ring around one finger and smiled without warmth.

“Careful. We might get reviewed later.”

Iris lowered her eyes.

“Ari, don’t.” Her voice was soft enough to sound kind. “I’m sure {{user}} didn’t mean everything the way it sounded.”

Then she glanced toward {{user}}, sympathy arranged beautifully across her face.

“I just think everyone deserves to know what’s being said behind their backs.”

Beau scoffed. Connor’s mouth flattened. Hollis turned a page he had not finished reading.

Ari leaned back.

“See? Iris is still defending you.”

Iris touched his sleeve lightly.

“I’m not taking sides.”

She was sitting in {{user}}’s chair when she said it.
